newsitem.title: GERMANY: Focus - Schering welcomes Japan pill news.
newsitem.headline: Focus - Schering welcomes Japan pill news.

text.p: German drug maker Schering AG said on Wednesday that a Japanese government report saying oral contraceptive pills were safe was a "step in the right direction" towards lifting a ban on the Pill in Japan.
The Pill, a vital component in the sexual revolution in Western society, has been banned in Japan since its introduction 30 years ago.
Schering is one of the world's largest manufacturers of oral contraceptives, and a spokeswoman said it expected a full decision on whether the ban would be lifted by mid-1997.

At the same time, the spokeswoman disputed one estimate that put the the potential Japanese oral contraceptive market at 500 million pound ($818 million), saying the true value of the market was "much lower".
Speculation that the Japanese government may drop its ban lifted shares in Schering to an all-time high in bourse trade, rising 8.80 marks, or 6.02 percent, to 155 marks.
Schering shares were top gainers in IBIS electronic trade, ending the day up 6.10 marks, or 4.17 percent, at 152.30 marks. The overall market ended up 0.36 percent at 3,245.02 points.
There are three committees in Japan which must examine the contraception issue, the Schering spokeswoman said.
The first committee gave its approval on November 19, Schering said. The second committee, which examined the ethical and moral aspects of the issue, gave its approval on Tuesday.
Schering said it did not not know when the final committee, which examines general health issues, would report but it expects a decision by the middle of the year.
The company said it was one of up to 10 companies who had applied for approval for low-hormone pills, and said it was seeking approval for its Triquilar combination product.
Ronald Koehler, an analyst at BHF Bank, said the news of a possible lifting of the ban was good news for Schering, but could be somewhat over-interpreted.
"There is not very high acceptance of the Pill in Asia -- for example it has a penetration of only three percent in Korea. A cultural revolution in Japan is probably needed," said Koehler.
Markus Rausch at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London said the news from Japan was only one factor boosting the share.
"The sales growth from a possible new marketing opportunity in Japan would in no way justify today's 500 million mark ($299.7 million) rise in Schering's market capitalisation," said Rausch.

Analysts reckoned that the removal of the ban on the Pill in Japan could generate around 100 million marks turnover for Schering, as the group could be required to manufacture the oral contraceptive with a Japanese partner.
"Set against total turnover of around six billion marks this is not so important," said Rausch.

Rausch said that reports on Tuesday that Schering planned to increase turnover by developing its therapeutics and its hormone preparation business were having a more positive effect on the share price.
Analysts cited reports that the group planned to increase sales by 850 million marks through new products in the next three years.
"Up until now the market thought that Schering had no new products in the pipeline," said Rausch.
